nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1}$ be pairwise distinct elements of $F$, and let $p \in F[X]$ be a nonzero polynomial. Then the number of indices $i < n$ with $p(\alpha_i) = 0$ is at most the degree of $p$.
nodes.title: Root count at distinct points

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ and let $k$ be a natural number. The Reed-Solomon code $\mathrm{RS}(\alpha, k)$ is the linear code of length $n$ over $F$ consisting of the words $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ for the polynomials $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$.
nodes.title: Reed-Solomon code

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct, let $k \le n$, put $t = \lfloor (n-k)/2 \rfloor$, and let $S$ be a solver for the key equations with error budget $t$. For every polynomial $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$ and every error word $\varepsilon \in F^n$ with at most $t$ nonzero entries, the Berlekamp-Welch decoder with solver $S$, run on the received word…
nodes.title: Berlekamp-Welch corrects every error of weight at most $\lfloor (n-k)/2 \rfloor$

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct, let $k, e$ be natural numbers with $2e + k \le n$, and let $S$ be a solver for the key equations with error budget $e$. For every received word $y \in F^n$, the Berlekamp-Welch decoder with solver $S$ reports failure on $y$ if and only if, for every polynomial $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$, the Hamming distance between $y$…
nodes.title: The decoder fails exactly when no codeword is close

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct, let $k, e$ be natural numbers with $2e + k \le n$ (the unique-decoding regime), and let $S$ be a solver for the key equations with error budget $e$. For every polynomial $p \in F[X]$ and every received word $y \in F^n$, the Berlekamp-Welch decoder with solver $S$ returns $p$ on $y$ if and only if $p$ has degree less than $k$ and the…
nodes.title: What the decoder returns

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, let $k, e$ be natural numbers and let $S$ be a solver for the key equations with error budget $e$. On a received word $y \in F^n$ the decoder runs $S$ on $y$ and reports failure if $S$ returns nothing. If $S$ returns a pair $(Q, E)$ (the solver guarantees that $E$ is monic), let $q$ be the quotient of $Q$ by $E$; the decoder returns $q$ if $q$ has…
nodes.title: Berlekamp-Welch decoder

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k, e$ be natural numbers with $2e + k \le n$. Let $p \in F[X]$ have degree less than $k$, and let $y \in F^n$ be within Hamming distance $e$ of $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$. If $(Q, E)$ solves the key equations for $y$ ($E$ is monic of degree $e$, $\deg Q < e + k$, and $Q(\alpha_i) = y_i E(\alpha_i)$ for all…
nodes.title: The quotient of a key-equation solution is the message

nodes.summary: For a field $F$ and points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, the $F$-linear map $F[X] \to F^n$ sending a polynomial $p$ to $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$.
nodes.title: Reed-Solomon encoder as a linear map

nodes.summary: For a field $F$ and points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, the encoding of a polynomial $p \in F[X]$ is the word $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ in $F^n$.
nodes.title: Reed-Solomon encoder

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k, e$ be natural numbers with $2e + k \le n$. Let $p \in F[X]$ have degree less than $k$, and let $y \in F^n$ be within Hamming distance $e$ of $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$. If $(Q, E)$ solves the key equations for $y$ ($E$ is monic of degree $e$, $\deg Q < e + k$, and $Q(\alpha_i) = y_i E(\alpha_i)$ for all…
nodes.title: Every solution of the key equations reveals the message

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ (not necessarily distinct) and let $1 \le k \le n$. There is a nonzero polynomial $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$ whose encoding $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ has at most $n - k + 1$ nonzero coordinates.
nodes.title: A low-weight Reed-Solomon codeword

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ and let $p \in F[X]$ have degree less than $k$. If a received word $y \in F^n$ differs from the encoding $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ in at most $e$ coordinates, then the Berlekamp-Welch key equations for $y$ with parameters $k$ and $e$ have a solution $(Q, E)$.
nodes.title: The key equations are solvable

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \le n$. The Reed-Solomon code of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has dimension $k$ over $F$.
nodes.title: Dimension of a Reed-Solomon code

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \le n$. If two polynomials $p, q \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$ satisfy $p(\alpha_i) = q(\alpha_i)$ for every $i < n$, then $p = q$.
nodes.title: The Reed-Solomon encoder is injective on low-degree polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$, let $k, e \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $y \in F^n$ be a received word. A pair of polynomials $(Q, E)$ over $F$ solves the key equations for $y$ when $E$ is monic of degree $e$, $Q$ has degree less than $e + k$, and $Q(\alpha_i) = y_i E(\alpha_i)$ for every $i < n$.
nodes.title: Berlekamp-Welch key equations

nodes.summary: For a field $F$, points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ and parameters $k, e \in \mathbb{N}$, a solver for the Berlekamp-Welch key equations is a procedure that takes a received word $y \in F^n$ and either returns a pair of polynomials $(Q, E)$ over $F$ or reports failure, such that every returned pair solves the key equations for $y$, and a pair is returned whenever the key equations for $y$ have a solution.
nodes.title: Solver for the key equations

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \le n$. For every nonzero polynomial $p \in F[X]$ of degree less than $k$, the encoding $(p(\alpha_0), \dots, p(\alpha_{n-1}))$ has at least $n - k + 1$ nonzero coordinates.
nodes.title: Nonzero Reed-Solomon codewords are heavy

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. The Reed-Solomon code of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has minimum distance at least $\max(n - k, 0) + 1$.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the minimum distance of a Reed-Solomon code

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $1 \le k \le n$. The Reed-Solomon code $C$ of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has minimum distance $d = n - \dim C + 1$, so the Singleton bound $d \le n - \dim C + 1$ for linear codes holds with equality.
nodes.title: Reed-Solomon codes meet the Singleton bound

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field (not necessarily finite), let $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1} \in F$ be pairwise distinct and let $1 \le k \le n$. The Reed-Solomon code of the points $\alpha$ with parameter $k$ has minimum distance exactly $n - k + 1$.
nodes.title: Reed-Solomon codes are MDS

nodes.summary: For points $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1}$ in a field $F$ and natural numbers $k$ and $e$, this is the solver for the key equations that, on a received word $y \in F^n$, returns a pair $(Q, E)$ of polynomials solving the key equations for $y$ (that is, $E$ is monic of degree $e$, $\deg Q < e + k$ and $Q(\alpha_i) = y_i E(\alpha_i)$ for all $i$), picked by the axiom of choice, whenever such a pair exists, and…
nodes.title: A key-equation solver by choice

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
